title: Deterministic discovery: explicit bundles and reviewed carrier tags
purpose: Separate premise selection, semantic identification, proof search and unsupported countermodel vocabulary on existing corpus statements. This is a fixed evaluation workload, not a proposition registry or a proof oracle.

measurement.unit: one target and one supplied or ranked premise bundle
deterministic_observations: requested and actual candidate statement IDs
coverage of the selected reference bundle
outer binders and their authored sense tags
proved, minimal-premise IDs, filters and certification verdict
known-route versus previously reported unregistered relationship
informational_only: wall-clock seconds on the shared runner
measurement.comparison: Use the same source baseline, solver, budget and infrastructure. Separate unchanged-engine before/after curation from ranked-versus-explicit input selection. An explicit bundle bypasses ranking; its success is not an improvement in ranking accuracy. Record source/artifact identities and retain raw reports outside tracked source.
measurement.unavailable: Missing toolchains or failed extraction are unavailable evidence, not unresolved logical goals or successful runs.
measurement.novelty_exclusions: None of these cases can count as a genuinely new philosophical relationship: the positive reference routes are registered or previously recorded in an attempt. A kernel-checked candidate remains conditional on its open premises and changes no corpus record or frontier status. Do not pass the cited Solution theorem to discovery as a premise or hint.
measurement.budget_rationale: 10000 heartbeats (in the CLI's thousands unit) was chosen before execution to bound equal-budget comparisons on narrow known consequences, with an explicit hard-solver control. It was not tuned against outcomes. Historical attempts quoted below used their separately stated budgets.
